definition: Small text files stored on your device by websites to remember information about your visits, preferences, and activities across browsing sessions.
metaDescription: Learn about cookies - small files websites store on your device to remember login info, preferences, and track your browsing for personalized experiences.
simpleExplanation: Think of cookies as digital sticky notes that websites leave on your computer. When you visit a site, it might save a cookie to remember you're logged in, what's in your shopping cart, or your language preference so you don't have to re-enter this information every time.
whyItMatters: Cookies can enhance your browsing experience with personalized content and convenience, but they also enable extensive tracking of your online behavior. Understanding cookies helps you make informed decisions about your privacy and control what information websites can collect about you.
technicalDetail: Cookies are HTTP headers sent between browsers and servers, containing key-value pairs with optional attributes like expiration dates, domains, and security flags. They're automatically included in subsequent requests to the same domain, enabling stateful interactions in the otherwise stateless HTTP protocol.

examples.explanation: When you add items to an online shopping cart but don't complete the purchase, a cookie remembers your selections so they're still there when you return to the site later.
After logging into your email or social media account, a session cookie keeps you logged in as you navigate different pages, so you don't have to re-enter your password constantly.
Ad networks use cookies to track which websites you visit and build a profile of your interests, allowing them to show you targeted advertisements across different sites.
